summary: Record final Metal scheduling measurements, focused correctness evidence and the bounded routine smoke without advancing full parity qualification.
regressions: 24 native runtime tests, Rust fmt/clippy, focused fresh-Rust scheduling/search/refit cases, exact eight-frame mesh/joint schedule comparison and six-frame Balls active-state comparison passed.
Routine Metal smoke passed 71 regressions and 11 representative physics cases in 238.766 seconds with the unchanged 290-second budget.
differences: Same-input initial Balls debug testbed step fell from 27.911 to 5.792 ms; repeated 30-frame stage replay medians fell from about 23.05 to 4.05-4.16 ms. No current Rust timing or settled-pile performance claim.
Native indirect/swap scheduling is Metal-specific. The khal-style virtual-grid fallback is documented but not implemented or qualified for TileLang CUDA/Ascend.

Small hub/round capacity grids and the fusion capacity heuristic remain. Change 0127 production-reference divergence remains blocking; full matrix and reconciliation were not run, and the full baseline remains stale.
